definitions.gloss: nursing; tending to; looking after (someone sick, injured, or intoxicated)
definitions.explanation: The act of caring for someone who is ill, hurt, or incapacitated, especially providing immediate or personal assistance. Often used for informal caregiving rather than professional medical care.

examples.japanese: ⟦{酔|よ}った→酔う：14437_you⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{介抱|かいほう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I looked after my drunk friend.

examples.japanese: ⟦{倒|たお}れた→倒れる：01160_taoreru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{介抱|かいほう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{現|あらわ}れた→現れる：01870_arawareru⟧。
examples.english: Someone quickly appeared to tend to the person who collapsed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一晩中|ひとばんじゅう}→一晩中：20338_hitobanjuu⟧⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{介抱|かいほう}⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: She spent all night nursing her sick child.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{介抱|かいほう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is used as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb meaning "to nurse, to tend to."

USAGE:
{介抱|かいほう} often implies personal, hands-on care in an immediate situation — helping someone who has collapsed, nursing a drunk person, or tending to someone who is suddenly ill. It differs from ⟦{看護|かんご}→看護：13668_kango⟧ (professional nursing) and ⟦{介護|かいご}→介護：04805_kaigo⟧ (long-term caregiving).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{酔|よ}っ{払|ぱら}い→酔っ払い：09429_yopparai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{介抱|かいほう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to look after a drunk person)
- ⟦{怪我人|けがにん}→怪我人：23513_keganin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{介抱|かいほう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to tend to an injured person)
